model.rationale: The fundamentals point decisively Democratic: the redrawn district carries a solid partisan lean, and Solis's fundraising and name recognition far exceed those of Republican Pedro Casas, who reports no financial activity. Markets and the partisan environment both corroborate a comfortable Democratic margin.

overview:
This open Southern California seat was redrawn after the 2020 census to lean Democratic, with a partisan advantage of about eight points for that party. With no incumbent on the ballot, the race features Democrat Hilda Solis, a prominent former county and federal official, against Republican Pedro Casas.

Solis has raised more than $1 million and holds a cash advantage, while Casas reports no fundraising activity and no outside groups have spent against her. Prediction markets price a Democratic victory at roughly 94 percent. With no public polling available, the forecast rests on district fundamentals, which point to a Democratic win of roughly twenty points.
